assumptions: System states require normalization against a noise baseline to distinguish divergent signal.
Internal coupling coefficients modulate state transition regimes.
Observable divergence magnitude is a function of coupling sensitivity.
definition.falsification: If the normalized divergence ratio remains < 0.3 across all coupling test conditions (0.0 to 1.0), the sensitivity hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when internal coupling coefficients exceed a critical threshold, relative to a noise-baseline. The divergence ratio is therefore a function of the system's sensitivity to perturbation, normalized against stochastic variance.
definition.uncertainty: Normalization methods against stochastic noise may inadvertently mask true divergence; this threshold must be empirically bracketed.

definition.reason: Previous measurement was invalid; the hypothesis needs refinement and the experiment requires better normalization.
definition.stop_condition: Failure to demonstrate consistent divergence ratio above 0.3 after three replications.
definition.uncertainty: The critical coupling threshold remains unknown and requires controlled experimentation to establish.

proposal.summary: Revising the divergent values hypothesis (hyp-divergent-values-002) to address experimental measurement failure by clarifying the divergence normalization methodology and tightening falsification constraints to distinguish signal from stochastic noise.
proposal.title: Path Dependence and Divergent Values: Hypothesis Revision
